reading.body:
Delaware passed data center and large energy use facility laws in August 2026, then saw a data center moratorium introduced the following June.

The pattern is a state moving in both directions at once. SB312 amended Titles 9, 22, and 29 on data centers, and HB233 amended Title 26 on large energy use facilities, both passing on 2026-08-25. SB353, a moratorium on data center development, was introduced on 2026-06-29 and has not passed. The same session produced HB450 on land use and HB500, a capital improvements bond act. Read together, Delaware is writing the rules for siting and powering large facilities while a faction tries to stop new ones.

For AI specifically, the energy and siting bills are the ones that touch compute. A data center is a building, and a large energy use facility is a load on the grid, so legislation naming both is legislation about the physical layer of AI. The AI-specific bills in the list are narrower: HB404 creates a pilot program for AI and extended reality in schools, HJR7 directs the AI Commission to build a regulatory sandbox for agentic AI, and HB16 amends the AI Commission itself. None of these govern compute directly.

The list does not say how much power Delaware data centers draw, whether SB312 or HB233 constrain or enable construction, or what the moratorium would cover. It also does not show the text of any bill, only titles and statuses. The single news item concerns a federal appellate fair use ruling on AI training, which is a copyright matter and not a Delaware law.
